The live labs reconstruct the operator in the browser. Posted residuals stay on X. Recurrence is not a unification proof.

def recover(G, R, shock, tau_lo=0.25, tau_hi=0.72):
    stress = strain(G, R, shock)
    keep   = G[stress < tau_lo]
    warp   = deform(G[(stress >= tau_lo) & (stress < tau_hi)], R)
    reseed = reset(G[stress >= tau_hi])
    return splice(keep, warp, reseed)

Codazzi thread (1 Aug 2026)

The figure post is the question. The GitHub folder is the harness. Same-day Grok reviews and a genericity closeout sit on the same conversation. Finite three-spin exponential family only. Not gravity, not all graphs.

Can a canonical information-theoretic response geometry always be generated from a single scalar potential? After building the framework from first principles, deriving the mathematics, and creating an executable verification harness, the smallest canonical interacting model says no. The result isn’t “we found gravity.” The result is that potential information geometry and response information geometry can separate.

Six minutes later Aaron handed Grok the August 2026 scientific status report and the uqcf_codazzi_proof folder.

Model (eight-state enumeration, h3 = 0):

p_{\theta,J}(x)=\frac{1}{Z(\theta,J)}\exp\bigl[h_1 x_1+h_2 x_2+J(x_1 x_2+x_2 x_3+x_3 x_1)\bigr],\quad x_i\in\{\pm 1\}

Pulled-back bidirectionally symmetrized response tensor and its exponential-affine Codazzi defect. Weak-coupling susceptibility already on the Supported ledger:

\Xi(J)=J^2\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}+O(J^3)

Exact closed-form susceptibility at h=0, Grok-verified against high-precision numerical differentiation:

\Xi^{\mathrm{sym}}(J)=\begin{pmatrix}-A(J)&B(J)\\-B(J)&A(J)\end{pmatrix}

A(J)=\frac{8(e^J-1)^3(e^J+1)^3(e^{2J}+1)^3(7e^{4J}+1)}{(e^{4J}+3)^5}

B(J)=\frac{32(e^J-1)^2(e^J+1)^2(e^{2J}+1)^2(e^{8J}+2e^{4J}+5)e^{4J}}{(e^{4J}+3)^6}

For every finite real J≠0, B(J)>0, so the susceptibility is nonzero. Near J=0, det Ξ^{sym}(J)=J^4+O(J^5)>0. The Codazzi defect is therefore not identically zero. Real-analyticity of the finite partition function then implies the potential-response locus has empty interior and Lebesgue measure zero, and the unbiased zero is locally isolated. That is the genericity theorem inside this model. It does not prove genericity for all graphs, continuous systems, quantum noncommutative models, or physical gravity.
